draft.title: Matrix operations
card: A matrix is a rectangle of numbers in rows and columns. Its order is rows × columns, so a matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns has order 2 × 3.
To add matrices, they must have the same order. Add the entries in matching positions. To scale a matrix, multiply every entry by the number.
To multiply A × B, the number of columns in A must equal the number of rows in B. The result has A's rows and B's columns.
Each entry of the product is a row of A times a column of B: multiply in pairs, then add. Example: (2 3) × (4 5)ᵀ, where the column is 4 then 5, gives 2×4 + 3×5 = 23.
draft.remember: Add needs equal orders. Multiply needs columns of the first to equal rows of the second.

a.q: Matrix A has order 2 × 3 and matrix B has order 3 × 4. What is the order of A × B?
a.why: The columns of A (3) match the rows of B (3), so the product exists. It has the rows of A and the columns of B, so its order is 2 × 4. Order 3 × 3 comes from taking the matching numbers instead.

b.q: A shop sells 2 items. Row matrix P = (10 20) holds the prices in dollars. Column matrix Q holds the numbers sold on one day: 3 of the first item and 4 of the second. What does P × Q give?
opts: 110, the total number of items sold
30, the total price of the two items
b.why: P × Q = 10×3 + 20×4 = 30 + 80 = 110, which is price times number sold, added up: the takings in dollars. Adding 3 + 4 gives the items sold, 7, not 110.
b.clue: Multiply in pairs, then add the results.
